title: Bees Cook Giant Hornets Alive Without a Single Sting

scenes.text: Bees can cook a giant hornet alive. No sting needed.
A giant hornet can wipe out a whole hive in hours. But Japanese honeybees have a trick.
Hundreds of them swarm the hornet and wrap it in a tight ball.
They shiver their flight muscles, and within minutes the ball reaches 46 degrees Celsius.
The hornet dies at that heat, helped by the carbon dioxide the bees breathe out. The bees can stand about five degrees more.
No sting. Just a ball of bees. Cooked alive.

description:
Bees can cook a giant hornet alive, with no sting at all.
Japanese honeybees wrap an invading hornet in a tight ball and shiver their muscles until the ball reaches about 46 degrees Celsius. Heat plus the carbon dioxide they breathe out kills the hornet in minutes, while the bees can stand about five degrees more.
Would you want to be in that ball?
first_comment: Bees or hornets: who is the real villain here?
